result.title: Does Location Matter? A Black-Box Causal Audit Reveals Model-Dependent Audio Grounding in LALM Hallucination
result.comment: 5 pages, 1 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to IEEE ICASSP 2027
result.summary: Large audio-language models (LALMs) frequently exhibit object hallucination, affirming absent sounds. The dominant mitigation, Audio-Aware Decoding (AAD), contrasts logits under real audio against an all-zero "blank" waveform, flagged by prior review as out-of-distribution. We introduce a black-box causal test that isolates the claimed evidence itself: localize a claim's evidence region via CLAP similarity, remove it by spectral gating, and compare against a random-window control across a 2x2x2 grid on three LALMs. On Qwen2-Audio-7B, localized ablation's raw AUROC trails blank's (0.613 vs. 0.721); this is a duration confound, not a localization failure, since blank removes the entire clip versus the grid's 2-4 s. Holding duration fixed, localization beats random removal at every cell on both models. Raw detection value remains model-dependent, especially on Audio Flamingo 3. The same evidence corrects decoding: contrastive decoding combining blank and language-prior contrasts, gated and ensembled, raises Qwen2-Audio accuracy from 57.1% to 71.9%, beating AAD alone. A unified causal-grounding profile does not transfer between models, indicating different grounding regimes. The source code and a detailed report of our findings, including identified limitations, are available at https://github.com/khalooei/causa.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一种黑箱因果审计：用 CLAP 相似度定位声明对应的音频证据区域，以谱门控移除并与随机窗口对照，在三个 LALM 上检验音频 grounding 的真实贡献，并指出时长混杂；还据此把 blank 与语言先验对比解码门控集成，提升检测准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 「定位证据—移除—随机对照—控制混杂」的审计思路可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正依赖视觉证据、而非坍缩为语言先验；但对象为音频幻觉，能否迁移到视觉推理仍需核查。
